record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For each dimension m, let alpha_m be the smallest threshold such that P_{ij,k} > alpha_m for every heredity coefficient forces an arbitrary QSO on S^{m-1} to be regular. It is known that P_{ij,k} > 1/(2m) is sufficient for regularity and that alpha_2 = (3 - sqrt(7))/2. What are the exact values of alpha_m for every m >= 3?

evidence.quote: In [17] the authors consider an arbitrary QSO V : S m−1 → S m−1 with matrix P = (Pij,k ) and studied the problem of finding the smallest αm such that the condition Pij,k > αm implies the regularity of V . Theorem 7. [17] 1) If Pij,k > 1/2m then V is regular. 2) α2 = 1/2 (3 − √7).
Problem 12. Find exact values of αm for any m ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 2$ be an integer and let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the standard $(m-1)$-simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
\[
(Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,
\]
where the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy $P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$. The operator $V$ is called regular if for every initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$ the iterates $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$ converge to a single fixed point of $V$ that does not depend on $x^{(0)}$.

For each $m\ge 2$, define $\alpha_m$ to be the smallest real number with the property that the condition $P_{ij,k}>\alpha_m$ for every triple $(i,j,k)$ forces every such QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ to be regular. It is known that $P_{ij,k}>1/(2m)$ suffices to ensure regularity (so $\alpha_m\le 1/(2m)$) and that $\alpha_2=(3-\sqrt{7})/2$.

Determine the exact value of $\alpha_m$ for every $m\ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on quadratic stochastic operators, with the value known only for $m=2$ and a sufficient bound $1/(2m)$. A targeted web search returned no source reporting exact values of $\alpha_m$ for any $m\ge 3$, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing regularity conditions for QSOs on the simplex; lists open problems including determination of sharp thresholds.
status_evidence.claim: The exact value of the regularity threshold for QSOs is known only in low dimension; higher-dimensional cases remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Regularity of Diagonally Positive Quadratic Doubly Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity of quadratic doubly stochastic operators with diagonally positive cubic stochastic matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work on QSO regularity has not produced exact thresholds $\alpha_m$ for $m\ge 3$.
